parties:
Hriday Ranjan Das
Vs.
Nihar Bala Das & Ors
full_judgment:
3. Mr. B.B. Roy Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant has taken me through the judgment appealed against and other materials on record. The learned advocate submits that the plaintiff has filed this suit for possession on the basis of a absolute title but it is evident that on the strength of his purchase at the mortgage execution. Sristidhar from whom the plaintiff traces her title could acquire only the mortgagor's right to the equity of redemption in the suit land inasmuch as the Kot mortgagee Prankrishna was not impleaded in the mortgage suit. The plaintiff had not acquired the absolute title which she claimed. The learned advocate further submits that the suit for possession on the basis of a title which the plaintiff had claimed was also time barred inasmuch as neither Sristidhar nor Akhil and Haradas who purchased from him not plaintiff who purchased from Akhil and Hardas could ever get possession of the suit land and plaintiff or her predecessors were never in possession within the period of limitation. The learned advocate submits that the learned Subordinate Judge has given the plaintiff a decree on the basis of a title to the equity of redemption which she did not claim and in regard to which she had not made out a case in the plaint. The learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in doing so and his judgment cannot be sustained. The point raised by Mr. B. R. Roy Chowdhury is well taken. The appellants in the instant case, however, stand on a much stronger ground to which I now pass on. 

 4. Hridoy son of Jagabhandu filed two redemption suits for redemption of the Kot mortgages in 1952. In those suits Chandra Bala was impleaded as defendant (defdt No. 10 in redemption suit No. 13 of 1952 and defendant No. 11 in redemption suit no. 14 of 1952). Chandra Bala filed written statement to resist the claim of redemption of Hridoy in the two plots of the present suit on the ground that the right to redemption in those plots has passed to her on the basis of auction purchase of Sristidhar and on the basis of her title traced from Sristidhar. In those suits she also filed separate applications for being transposed as co-plaintiff and for giving her the relief of redemption. In an analogous judgment passed in those suits the learned Munsif found that she (Chandra Bala) acquired limited right in the equity of redemption in the said plots which she could no longer enforce as it was barred by limitation. On this finding the learned Munsif rejected her petitions for transposition and evidently her claim for redemption also. The suits were decreed for redemption against the heirs of the Kot mortgagee though it was dismissed against Chandra Bala. In a suit for redemption in the case of a dispute about the title to the equity of redemption between two rival claimants, in the instant case between Hridoy and Chandra Bala, the question as to whether Chandra Bala had any title to the equity of redemption in the two plots of the present suit was directly and substantially in issue. In the judicial determination of the question as to whether Chandra Bala should be transposed as a co-plaintiff as prayed for by her in the petitions for transposition in the earlier redemption suits, the question, as to whether she had title to the equity of redemption in the two plots in question was directly and substantially in issue, and a decision in those suits that Chandra Bala had no such right operates as res-judicata when the same question comes up for judicial determination in the present suit. As such Chandrabala or her heir Niharbala was not entitled to claim any title to the equity of redemption in the present suit and the learned lower appellate court was not entitled to find title in her on the basis of her such title and pass a decree in her favour's on the basis.
